state.target_passage: Your two-point thermal check, the dual-salt humidity audit, the wind-gated pressure comparison, and especially the monthly weigh-and-measure rain-gauge verification close the calibration loop in exactly the way I needed it closed—logging the *offset* as a sliding two-week median rather than a single number is the right move because it converts a slow creep into a visible trend line in the instrument table that a weekly QC glance can catch before it contaminates a monthly mean, and the Norfolk corrosion narrative you've pinned to that protocol is precisely the scenario where a naïve "compare to factory spec once a year" scheme would have let forty-five millimetres of seasonal deficit masquerade as orographic undercatch. What I'm locking in now, building directly on your calibration cadence, is the **sampling architecture and the minimum-observability rule** that governs when a derived product is permitted to exist in the record. The backbone is an automated datalogger on the mast sampling all four channels at one-minute intervals continuously—this is non-negotiable and independent of any human presence; the observer's scheduled 0600 and 1800 LST visits are not the data source but the *verification and quality-flag-assignment* event, during which the observer cross-checks the raw sensor outputs against a handheld spot-reading, visually inspects for fouling or insect activity, and stamps quality flags 0–2 on the preceding twelve hours of automated rows. On top of that baseline I'm mandating an **event-triggered supplemental mode**: if the datalogger detects a rate-of-change threshold—temperature change ≥ 2 °C in thirty minutes, barometric fall ≥ 3 hPa in two hours, or tip-rate exceeding 15 tips per minute—the unit steps up to continuous one-minute logging of all channels for six hours and pushes a notification to the on-call observer, so that a frontal passage or convective burst is captured at full temporal resolution rather than at the two-reading-per-day grid. Critically, no derived product—hourly mean, daily mean, monthly mean, seasonal total—is computed or written to the shared drive unless at least eighty percent of the expected one-minute records in that aggregation window carry quality flags 0–2; below that threshold the product row is suppressed entirely and a dedicated gap row (quality flag 5, "sufficient data not available") is appended to the observation table citing the window's actual fill percentage and the reason code drawn from the site-conditions table. If no on-call observer is available for two consecutive scheduled verification visits, the station enters auto-only mode: data continues to log, every row is flagged 3 (unverified), and a site-conditions anomaly row records the observer's absence reason so the gap is *documented* rather than invisible. The failure I want us to engineer around, because it exploits the exact seam between the verification schedule and the event-triggered logic, is **asymmetric time-of-day sampling collapse concentrated on the most meteorologically extreme window**.
